answer: Every physical machine's quartz oscillator drifts at its own tiny rate. Verifiers ask agents to sign timestamps at random moments and plot each one's clock skew over days. Clones on one server mirror the exact same drift curve, so the protocol merges them into a single identity with one reward. Faking distinct skews over a weeks-long horizon means renting genuinely separate hardware, which makes a sybil swarm cost as much as honest agents.
